sec: Genetic syndromes associated with DM and MODY

items.q: Match the genetic syndrome to its printed feature — 1) Type A resistance 2) Type B resistance 3) Rabson–Mendenhall syndrome … A) Seen in females, acanthosis nigricans and hyperandrogenism B) Type A plus PCOS and HAIR-AN syndrome C) Childhood DM, acanthosis, rapidly growing hair and abnormal dentition
items.exp: The table lists the respective feature sets for Type A resistance, Type B resistance and Rabson–Mendenhall syndrome. (Book p924)

items.q: The pathogenesis written for Type A resistance is:
items.exp: Type A resistance is paired with insulin-receptor resistance in the table. (Book p924)

items.q: Assess the resistance-syndrome table: I Type B resistance is linked to a post-binding defect in insulin action. II Rabson–Mendenhall syndrome is linked to insulin-receptor mutations.
items.exp: The pathogenesis column gives a post-binding defect for Type B and insulin-receptor mutations for Rabson–Mendenhall syndrome. (Book p924)

items.q: A child has diabetes, acanthosis nigricans, rapidly growing hair and abnormal dentition. Which syndrome does the page associate with this pattern?
items.exp: Those four findings are the feature list in the Rabson–Mendenhall row. (Book p924)

items.q: Type 4 DM is expanded on this page as middle age related DM, abbreviated ___.
items.exp: The Other Types of DM section labels Type 4 DM as middle age related DM (MARD). (Book p924)

items.q: Match the MODY feature to the exact note — 1) Inheritance 2) Insulin dependence 3) Age of manifestation 4) Renal transporter note … A) AD through at least 3 generations B) Not insulin dependent C) Before 25 years D) Decreased SGLT2 leading to glycosuria
items.exp: The MODY features are AD vertical transmission through at least three generations, not insulin dependent, before 25 years, and decreased SGLT2 with glycosuria. (Book p924)

items.q: MODY is written as manifesting before what age?
items.exp: The MODY feature list says it manifests before 25 years. (Book p924)

items.q: Assess the MODY notes: I The page says MODY has no complications. II The page describes an inappropriate beta-cell response to a rise in blood glucose.
items.exp: Both statements appear in the MODY section. (Book p924)

items.q: Match the MODY type to its defect or feature — 1) MODY 1 2) MODY 2 3) MODY 3 4) MODY 4 … A) HNF-4α B) Glucokinase C) HNF-1α D) IPF-1
items.exp: The MODY table pairs MODY 1 with HNF-4α, MODY 2 with glucokinase, MODY 3 with HNF-1α, and MODY 4 with IPF-1. (Book p924)

items.q: Which treatment is written for MODY 3 in the table?
items.exp: The MODY 3 row gives sulfonylureas as the treatment. (Book p924)

items.q: Which MODY type is marked as the most common in the table?
items.exp: MODY 3 is marked '(m/c)' in the table. (Book p924)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the listed MODY-5 features or associations?
items.exp: The table associates MODY 5 with renal cysts and genital anomalies; retinal detachment is not listed. (Book p924)
